body:
## Expected Behavior
After upgrading from v1.29.x to v1.30.x, the ringpop membership ring should
  converge within seconds of pods starting. Each service (frontend, history,
  matching, worker) should see only the currently running pods as reachable
  members, and inter-service gRPC calls should succeed normally.

## Actual Behavior
 After upgrading to v1.30.4, the cluster exhibits permanent ringpop membership
  churn (~4000 ring change events per 30 seconds). The membership ring sees
  17 members when only 4 pods are running — the extra 13 are zombie IPs from
  previous pod restarts still present in Cassandra. SWIM continuously pings
  these dead IPs, causing them to cycle alive→suspect→faulty indefinitely.
  This results in continuous EOF errors between frontend→matching and
  frontend→history, making workflow execution impossible. The cluster does
  not self-heal.
```
  Ring churn log (repeating ~140 times/second per pod):
  {"level":"debug","msg":"Received a ring changed event",
   "component":"service-resolver","service":"history",
   "logging-call-at":"common/membership/ringpop/service_resolver.go:252"}
```


  EOF errors between services:
```
  {"level":"error","msg":"matching client encountered error",
   "service":"frontend",
   "error":"connection error: desc = \"error reading server preface: EOF\"",
   "logging-call-at":"client/matching/metric_client.go:197"}
```


  Ring sees 17 members, only 4 pods running:
```
  {"level":"info","msg":"Current reachable members",
   "service":"matching",
   "addresses":["10.0.0.154:7235","10.0.0.155:7235", ...17 IPs total...]}
```
## Steps to Reproduce the Problem
    1. Run Temporal v1.29.x on Kubernetes with Cassandra backend and perform
       several rolling restarts (simulating normal operations/upgrade process),
       allowing stale pod IPs to accumulate in cluster_membership table
       (TTL = 48h)
    2. Upgrade to v1.30.x — commit f7ca7745 ("set page token during ringpop
       bootstrap") is now active, causing fetchCurrentBootstrapHostports() to
       correctly paginate and read ALL rows from cluster_membership instead of
       only the first page as in v1.29.x
    3. Observe all pods immediately exhibit ~4000 ring change events per 30
       seconds and inter-service EOF errors upon startup

## Specifications
    - Version: v1.30.4 (upgraded from v1.29.x)
    - Platform: Kubernetes with Cassandra persistence backend
    - Introduced by: commit f7ca7745 ("set page token during ringpop bootstrap")
    - Root cause: upsertMembershipRecordExpiryDefault = 48h in
      common/membership/ringpop/monitor.go allows stale pod IPs to accumulate
      across restarts; v1.29.x accidentally avoided this via the pagination bug;

      v1.30.x correctly reads all stale rows and injects them into SWIM
    - Proposed fix: reduce upsertMembershipRecordExpiryDefault from 48h to ~5m,
      or expose it as a configurable parameter

comments.body: Can confirm this after upgrading to v1.30.4 this morning... the cluster is still trying to connect (and failing) to old ECS tasks in our cluster after the deployment and checking the `cluster_membership` table, we have a lot of stale entries with `record_expiry` set to 48hrs ahead, which leads to the logs being flooded with failed connection attempts to the old IPs.

First, entries are kept in the cluster membership table for 48 hours for debugging purposes, but only records that have been updated in the last 20 seconds are passed to ringpop for bootstrap:

https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/v1.30.4/common/membership/ringpop/monitor.go#L347
https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/v1.30.4/common/membership/ringpop/monitor.go#L35

Can you look for the `bootstrap hosts fetched` log and see what's being passed there?
https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/v1.30.4/common/membership/ringpop/monitor.go#L369

Second, even if extra bootstrap hosts are passed to ringpop, that should only affect things for a few seconds and it should still converge to a stable set. If it's not doing that, then something is going wrong unrelated to bootstrap. If an address is showing up in `Current reachable members` then it must have responded to a ping at some point. Are those ips actually unused or is there something (maybe a new pod in another temporal cluster) that can respond to them?

Third, the issue in #8719 is separate: that's grpc connections being kept open after being removed from membership, and has nothing to do with ringpop bootstrap.

Bootstrap hosts analysis:
   All IPs in the bootstrap list are current, live pods with recent heartbeats
   — the Cassandra filtering on healthyHostLastHeartbeatCutoff = 20s is working
    correctly. No stale entries appear.
  
   The actual failure: The join duration itself exceeds maxJoinDuration: 30s,
   taking 44–52 seconds consistently. The pods successfully upsert their
   heartbeat, appear in the bootstrap list of peers, but ringpop cannot
   complete the join handshake within the 30s window. The bootstrap list
   contains ~20 hosts across multiple Kubernetes node pools (including pods on
   perftest-z1 nodes vs cpu-worker nodes). All history pods crash before they
   can form the ring, so none are listening on port 6934 when their peers
   attempt to connect.
  
   This is a pure ringpop join timeout issue. Is maxJoinDuration: 30s tunable,
   or is there a known issue with large bootstrap lists causing join latency?
   The 20-host bootstrap list may itself be contributing — ringpop is trying to
    contact all of them, and the cross-node-pool latency or connection
   concurrency may be pushing total join time past the threshold.

Thanks for the additional information. I still have a lot of questions to get to the bottom of this though...

So all the ips in the bootstrap list (`bootstrap hosts fetched`) are current? But you think the bootstrap list that you're seeing now is larger than it was before, and that might be causing problems?

It's a little hard to follow exactly what ringpop is doing in the "join", but it definitely looks like it should stop after finding one successful peer:
https://github.com/temporalio/ringpop-go/blob/b97329e994f792f70427a7533a3e7a98976eb262/swim/join_sender.go#L310-L320
https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/145f109050fa472bdfe8110770d955d0e12c65f4/common/membership/ringpop/monitor.go#L202
So I'm surprised that even a large bootstrap list would prevent it from resolving. I wonder if maybe even a _lower_ ParallelismFactor could help it converge faster in this case.

You said maybe cross-node-pool latency is a concern.. what exactly is the maximum ping latency between all of your nodes? Ringpop has lots of configurable timeouts but the defaults may be optimized for a lower latency environment than yours.

I can think of two things to try:
1. In the short term, you can just adjust the join duration in the static config, it would look like:
```yaml
global: 
  membership:
    maxJoinDuration: 60s
```
2. As a more general fix, we can try putting the rest of the bootstrap and other ringpop config knobs in the static config so you can play around with them. Also we could add an option to deliberately trim the bootstrap list to a smaller length before passing it to ringpop. I'm not sure anyone on the team can get to this soon, but we'd accept a PR for exposing more options or trimming the bootstrap list.

Experiencing the same issue in temporal version 1.31
probably after some pod restarts  - matching service & history service got a lot of "Network dial" errors to stale IP's which no longer existed, but still records still exist in the DB with an expiry of 48 hours. only after scaling down to 0 and waiting before scaling up the issue was solved. However this will probably happen again upon pod restarts.

title: Ringpop membership churn after upgrade to v1.30.x
